PRS.indicator: Trace a consolidated P&L problem back to the business unit or country actually driving it

scale.5: Traces a consolidated P&L problem to the unit or country actually driving it, not just where it surfaces.
scale.3: Traces a consolidated P&L problem to the unit closest to the symptom, not the one actually driving it.
scale.1: Overlooks which business unit or country actually drives a consolidated P&L problem, acting on the visible symptom instead.

PRS.indicator: Integrate data from across business units before diagnosing a problem that spans the organization

scale.5: Integrates data from across business units before diagnosing an organization-wide problem, closing gaps a narrower view would miss.
scale.3: Integrates data from the units closest to the problem, leaving other units' data unchecked when diagnosing organization-wide issues.
scale.1: Neglects to integrate data across business units before diagnosing an organization-wide problem, working from one unit's numbers alone.

PRS.indicator: Weigh competing explanations from business unit leaders before settling on an organization-wide problem's root cause

scale.5: Weighs competing explanations from business unit leaders before settling on an organization-wide problem's true root cause.
scale.3: Weighs competing explanations from business unit leaders but settles on whichever aligns with the prior year's plan.
scale.1: Overlooks competing explanations from business unit leaders, settling on an organization-wide problem's root cause without weighing them.

STG.indicator: Set organizational direction that aligns priorities across business units and countries

scale.5: Sets organizational direction that aligns priorities across every business unit and country over the multi-year horizon.
scale.3: Sets organizational direction that aligns priorities for business units already on plan but defers when countries diverge.
scale.1: Neglects to set organizational direction across business units, leaving countries without shared priorities.

STG.indicator: Weigh long-term tradeoffs against the organization's direction before committing resources

scale.5: Weighs long-term tradeoffs against the organization's direction before committing capital across business units.
scale.3: Weighs tradeoffs for the current planning cycle but defers the organization's longer-term direction.
scale.1: Overlooks long-term tradeoffs when committing resources, leaving the organization's direction exposed.

STG.indicator: Translate long-term direction into priorities other senior leaders can act on

scale.5: Translates long-term direction into clear priorities other senior leaders can act on without further guidance.
scale.3: Translates long-term direction into priorities for senior leaders but leaves the sequencing for them to work out.
scale.1: Fails to translate long-term direction into priorities, leaving other senior leaders without a clear plan.

INN.indicator: Champion new ventures that require backing across multiple business units

scale.5: Champions new ventures that require backing across multiple business units, absorbing the risk of early missteps.
scale.3: Champions new ventures within a single business unit but hesitates to back ones spanning several.
scale.1: Resists championing new ventures, leaving promising ideas without organizational backing.

INN.indicator: Question established practices that no longer serve the organization's direction

scale.5: Proactively questions established practices that no longer serve the organization's direction, retiring them before they cost more.
scale.3: Questions established practices only after a business unit raises the cost of keeping them.
scale.1: Accepts established practices without question, letting outdated methods persist across the organization.

INN.indicator: Support other leaders who take a risk on an unproven idea

scale.5: Actively supports other leaders who take a risk on an unproven idea, shielding them if it fails.
scale.3: Supports other leaders who take a risk once the idea already shows early results.
scale.1: Neglects to support other leaders who take a risk, leaving them exposed if it fails.

JDG.indicator: Base capital allocation decisions on rigorous financial and strategic analysis

scale.5: Anchors every capital allocation decision in rigorous financial and strategic analysis, protecting consolidated P&L integrity.
scale.3: Reviews financial analysis for major allocation calls but defers to precedent across smaller ones.
scale.1: Neglects rigorous analysis before capital allocation calls, exposing consolidated P&L to avoidable risk.

JDG.indicator: Set organizational direction despite sustained uncertainty across multiple countries

scale.5: Sets a clear organizational direction despite sustained multi-country uncertainty, giving every business unit a stable reference point.
scale.3: Sets direction for countries with a clearer outlook but defers where uncertainty remains widest.
scale.1: Resists setting organizational direction while multi-country uncertainty persists, leaving business units without a reference point.

JDG.indicator: Weigh long-term tradeoffs across business units before committing capital

scale.5: Weighs long-term tradeoffs across business units rigorously before committing capital, protecting consolidated P&L over the multi-year horizon.
scale.3: Compares tradeoffs across business units before committing capital but underweights the long-term horizon.
scale.1: Does not weigh long-term tradeoffs across business units before committing capital, exposing consolidated P&L to avoidable risk.

DRV.indicator: Push the organization toward multi-year strategic targets despite setbacks in one business unit or country

scale.5: Pushes the organization toward multi-year strategic targets despite setbacks in one business unit or country.
scale.3: Pushes the organization toward multi-year strategic targets when every business unit performs.
scale.1: Neglects organization-wide strategic targets once one business unit sets back, letting the whole plan slip.

DRV.indicator: Set a personal bar for the organization's results above what the capital plan strictly requires

scale.5: Sets a personal bar for the organization's results above what the capital plan strictly requires.
scale.3: Sets a personal bar for the organization's results that matches the capital plan.
scale.1: Does not set a personal bar above the capital plan's minimum for the organization's results.

DRV.indicator: Sustain organization-wide pace across a multi-year plan rather than a single strong business unit

scale.5: Sustains organization-wide pace across the full multi-year plan rather than one strong business unit, avoiding a late-stage fade.
scale.3: Sustains organization-wide pace through a strong opening year but fades as the multi-year plan continues.
scale.1: Struggles to sustain organization-wide pace beyond one strong business unit, fading well before the multi-year plan ends.

CSF.indicator: Understand which strategic accounts most affect consolidated P&L outcomes

scale.5: Understands which strategic accounts most affect consolidated P&L outcomes, prioritizing attention accordingly.
scale.3: Understands which strategic accounts affect a single business unit's results but not the consolidated picture.
scale.1: Overlooks which strategic accounts most affect consolidated P&L, spreading attention too thin.

CSF.indicator: Keep commitments made to major customers across business units

scale.5: Consistently keeps commitments made to major customers across business units, protecting the organization's reputation.
scale.3: Keeps commitments made to major customers in one business unit but loses track across others.
scale.1: Fails to keep commitments made to major customers, damaging trust across business units.

CSF.indicator: Build strategic partnerships that strengthen the organization's competitive position

scale.5: Builds strategic partnerships that strengthen the organization's competitive position across multiple countries.
scale.3: Builds strategic partnerships within one country but rarely extends them to others.
scale.1: Neglects to build strategic partnerships, leaving the organization's competitive position weaker.

SLF.indicator: Set sales and partnership targets across business units that balance growth against consolidated P&L

scale.5: Sets sales and partnership targets across business units that balance growth against consolidated P&L.
scale.3: Sets sales and partnership targets across business units based on growth alone, without weighing them against consolidated P&L.
scale.1: Overlooks consolidated P&L when setting sales and partnership targets across business units, chasing growth without a check.

SLF.indicator: Explain the organization's value proposition in terms that match different major account segments

scale.5: Explains the organization's value proposition in terms that match different major account segments, tailoring the pitch to each.
scale.3: Explains the organization's value proposition with the same pitch across every major account segment.
scale.1: Struggles to explain the organization's value proposition across major account segments, relying on a single generic pitch.

SLF.indicator: Negotiate a major partnership that protects consolidated margin while meeting the partner's core need

scale.5: Negotiates a major partnership that protects consolidated margin while meeting the partner's core need.
scale.3: Negotiates a major partnership that meets the partner's core need but gives up consolidated margin to close it.
scale.1: Struggles to negotiate a major partnership that protects consolidated margin, giving up terms rather than working toward them.

OPX.indicator: Set operating standards that hold consistently across every business unit

scale.5: Sets operating standards that hold consistently across every business unit, closing gaps before they compound.
scale.3: Sets operating standards for the units already performing well but leaves the rest inconsistent.
scale.1: Overlooks inconsistent operating standards across business units, letting gaps compound unchecked.

OPX.indicator: Use consolidated data to detect operational patterns across countries

scale.5: Uses consolidated data to detect operational patterns across countries before they become P&L problems.
scale.3: Uses country-level data to detect operational patterns but rarely consolidates it across countries.
scale.1: Neglects to use consolidated data, missing operational patterns until they surface as P&L problems.

OPX.indicator: Remove structural obstacles that slow execution across business units

scale.5: Removes structural obstacles that slow execution across business units, unblocking progress at the source.
scale.3: Removes structural obstacles once a business unit escalates them but rarely looks for them first.
scale.1: Fails to remove structural obstacles, letting execution stall across business units.

TMG.indicator: Set organization-wide priorities and delegate accountability to other senior leaders

scale.5: Sets organization-wide priorities and delegates real accountability to other senior leaders, freeing them to lead their own units.
scale.3: Sets organization-wide priorities but retains accountability rather than delegating it to other senior leaders.
scale.1: Neglects to delegate accountability alongside organization-wide priorities, forcing other senior leaders to escalate decisions upward.

TMG.indicator: Give other senior leaders candid, specific feedback on organizational performance

scale.5: Gives other senior leaders candid, specific feedback on organizational performance, linking it directly to consolidated results.
scale.3: Gives other senior leaders feedback on organizational performance but keeps it diplomatic rather than specific.
scale.1: Avoids giving other senior leaders candid feedback, letting organizational underperformance go unaddressed.

TMG.indicator: Sustain engagement and collaboration among senior leaders across the organization

scale.5: Sustains strong engagement and collaboration among senior leaders across the organization, turning competing agendas into shared strategy.
scale.3: Sustains collaboration among senior leaders across the organization but leaves engagement uneven across business units.
scale.1: Neglects engagement and collaboration among senior leaders, letting competing agendas fragment organizational strategy.

INS.indicator: Coach other senior leaders to build succession depth in their units

scale.5: Coaches other senior leaders to build succession depth in their units, reducing single-person risk.
scale.3: Coaches other senior leaders informally but does not build succession depth in their units.
scale.1: Neglects to coach other senior leaders, leaving succession depth thin across business units.

INS.indicator: Recognize other senior leaders' contributions in front of the organization

scale.5: Consistently recognizes other senior leaders' contributions in front of the organization, reinforcing what good looks like.
scale.3: Recognizes other senior leaders' contributions privately but rarely does so in front of the organization.
scale.1: Overlooks other senior leaders' contributions, leaving strong performance unacknowledged across the organization.

INS.indicator: Build a culture where senior leaders push each other toward top performance

scale.5: Builds a culture where senior leaders push each other toward top performance across every business unit.
scale.3: Builds this culture among senior leaders who already perform well but not among the rest.
scale.1: Neglects to build this culture, leaving senior leaders to push performance on their own.

COM.indicator: Explain organizational strategy to business unit leaders in terms that connect it to each unit's priorities

scale.5: Explains organizational strategy to business unit leaders in terms that connect it to each unit's priorities.
scale.3: Explains organizational strategy to business unit leaders by stating the directive without connecting it to each unit's priorities.
scale.1: Struggles to explain organizational strategy to business unit leaders, leaving them with the directive but no reasoning.

COM.indicator: Listen to concerns raised by business unit leaders fully before responding

scale.5: Listens to concerns raised by business unit leaders fully before responding, letting what they say shape the strategy.
scale.3: Listens to concerns raised by business unit leaders partway before responding, missing points raised later.
scale.1: Resists letting business unit leaders finish raising a concern, responding to only part of what was said.

COM.indicator: Keep business unit leaders engaged through a strategy update rather than losing their attention

scale.5: Keeps business unit leaders engaged through a strategy update by tying it to what matters to each unit.
scale.3: Delivers a strategy update to business unit leaders but loses their attention partway through.
scale.1: Struggles to keep business unit leaders engaged through a strategy update, losing their attention from the start.

COL.indicator: Bring business unit leaders across the organization into a joint plan before it affects their units

scale.5: Brings business unit leaders across the organization into a joint plan before it affects their units.
scale.3: Brings business unit leaders across the organization into a joint plan after it is set.
scale.1: Neglects to bring business unit leaders into a joint plan before it affects their units.

COL.indicator: Split shared organizational initiatives evenly across business units rather than let one carry them

scale.5: Splits shared organizational initiatives evenly across business units, watching for early signs one unit is carrying too much.
scale.3: Splits shared organizational initiatives evenly across business units at the outset but leaves them uneven once priorities shift.
scale.1: Avoids redistributing shared organizational initiatives across business units, letting one unit carry them.

COL.indicator: Work through a disagreement between business unit leaders rather than decide for them

scale.5: Works through a disagreement between business unit leaders, reaching a shared resolution every unit can act on.
scale.3: Works through a disagreement between business unit leaders on operational matters but decides on larger strategic ones.
scale.1: Resists working through a disagreement between business unit leaders, deciding for them instead.

INF.indicator: Win business unit leaders' support for a capital allocation decision

scale.5: Wins business unit leaders' support for a capital allocation decision by addressing each one's concerns directly.
scale.3: Wins support from business unit leaders who already favor the decision but not from the rest.
scale.1: Fails to win business unit leaders' support, stalling the capital allocation decision.

INF.indicator: Argue for own position with evidence that spans multiple business units

scale.5: Argues for own position with evidence that spans multiple business units, making the case irrefutable.
scale.3: Argues for own position with evidence from a single business unit rather than across all of them.
scale.1: Struggles to argue for own position, relying on assertion rather than evidence across business units.

INF.indicator: Stand firm on a decision when a business unit leader pushes back

scale.5: Stands firm on a decision when a business unit leader pushes back, holding the line without damaging trust.
scale.3: Stands firm on a decision only until a business unit leader pushes back a second time.
scale.1: Concedes a decision as soon as a business unit leader pushes back, undermining organizational direction.

NET.indicator: Build a working relationship with industry contacts and external stakeholders before the organization needs their help

scale.5: Builds a working relationship with industry contacts and external stakeholders before the organization needs their help.
scale.3: Builds a working relationship with industry contacts and external stakeholders only once the organization already needs their help.
scale.1: Neglects to build a working relationship with industry contacts and external stakeholders.

NET.indicator: Adjust own communication style to fit stakeholders across the organization, the industry and outside it

scale.5: Adjusts own communication style to fit stakeholders across the organization, the industry and outside it.
scale.3: Adjusts own communication style for internal senior leaders but uses the same approach with external industry contacts.
scale.1: Resists adjusting own communication style across the organization and the industry, using the same approach with every stakeholder.

NET.indicator: Use an existing industry relationship to unblock a strategic initiative for the organization

scale.5: Uses an existing industry relationship to unblock a strategic initiative for the organization.
scale.3: Uses an existing industry relationship to unblock a strategic initiative only after a formal request stalls.
scale.1: Overlooks existing industry relationships, routing every strategic request through formal channels alone.

RES.indicator: Sustain organizational focus through sustained multi-country uncertainty

scale.5: Sustains organizational focus through sustained multi-country uncertainty, keeping every business unit oriented on the plan.
scale.3: Sustains organizational focus while uncertainty is confined to one country but wavers once it spreads.
scale.1: Loses organizational focus once multi-country uncertainty sets in, leaving business units without direction.

RES.indicator: Handle a consolidated P&L setback without shifting blame to a business unit

scale.5: Handles a consolidated P&L setback without shifting blame to a business unit, owning the outcome directly.
scale.3: Handles a consolidated P&L setback calmly but privately holds one business unit responsible.
scale.1: Shifts blame to a business unit after a consolidated P&L setback, eroding trust across the organization.

RES.indicator: Model composure for other senior leaders during an organization-wide crisis

scale.5: Models composure for other senior leaders during an organization-wide crisis, steadying the room when it matters most.
scale.3: Models composure for other senior leaders during a single business unit's crisis but not an organization-wide one.
scale.1: Loses composure during an organization-wide crisis, leaving other senior leaders without a steady reference point.

LRN.indicator: Seek feedback from other senior leaders on own strategic decisions

scale.5: Actively seeks feedback from other senior leaders on own strategic decisions, adjusting direction when the case is strong.
scale.3: Seeks feedback from other senior leaders only after a strategic decision has already been announced.
scale.1: Avoids seeking feedback on own strategic decisions, missing early signals from other senior leaders.

LRN.indicator: Reflect on which strategic decisions worked across business units and why

scale.5: Reflects on which strategic decisions worked across business units and why, applying the pattern to the next one.
scale.3: Reflects on which strategic decisions worked in one business unit but rarely compares across others.
scale.1: Neglects to reflect on which strategic decisions worked, repeating the same mistakes across business units.

LRN.indicator: Apply lessons from one business unit's experience to organization-wide decisions

scale.5: Applies lessons from one business unit's experience to organization-wide decisions, avoiding the same setback elsewhere.
scale.3: Applies lessons from one business unit's experience back to that same unit but rarely elsewhere.
scale.1: Overlooks lessons from one business unit's experience, repeating the same setback in others.

ITG.indicator: Follow through on an organization-wide commitment even when it becomes costly across business units

scale.5: Follows through on an organization-wide commitment even when it becomes costly across business units.
scale.3: Follows through on an organization-wide commitment when low-cost but lets it slide across business units.
scale.1: Neglects an organization-wide commitment once it becomes costly, leaving business units to absorb the consequence.

ITG.indicator: Admit a mistake to the organization rather than let a business unit take the blame

scale.5: Admits a mistake to the organization rather than let a business unit take the blame.
scale.3: Admits a mistake to the organization once it is already obvious but stays quiet otherwise.
scale.1: Avoids admitting a mistake to the organization, letting a business unit take the blame.

ITG.indicator: Apply organization-wide standards the same way across every business unit regardless of results pressure

scale.5: Applies organization-wide standards the same way across every business unit regardless of results pressure.
scale.3: Applies organization-wide standards when results are on track but relaxes them under results pressure.
scale.1: Resists applying organization-wide standards evenly, relaxing them under results pressure.

INC.indicator: Give business unit leaders from different backgrounds equal airtime in an organization-wide discussion

scale.5: Gives business unit leaders from different backgrounds equal airtime in an organization-wide discussion.
scale.3: Gives business unit leaders airtime when they speak up but does not draw out quieter ones.
scale.1: Overlooks business unit leaders from different backgrounds, letting the same few voices dominate every organization-wide discussion.

INC.indicator: Adjust organization-wide policy to accommodate a specific need raised by a business unit

scale.5: Adjusts organization-wide policy to accommodate a specific need raised by a business unit.
scale.3: Accommodates a specific need raised by a business unit once but leaves organization-wide policy unchanged.
scale.1: Resists adjusting organization-wide policy for a business unit's specific need, expecting it to fit the existing policy instead.

INC.indicator: Draw on a business unit leader's different perspective when it conflicts with the majority view

scale.5: Draws on a business unit leader's different perspective when it conflicts with the majority view.
scale.3: Draws on a business unit leader's perspective when it agrees with the majority but sets it aside otherwise.
scale.1: Overlooks a business unit leader's different perspective whenever it conflicts with the majority view, dismissing it without consideration.
